record_identity.title: Tasmania Police Axon Draft One trial misattributed family-violence participants and omitted risks

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Tasmania Police 2025 Axon Draft One family-violence report-drafting trial
incident_identity.date_basis: The official study gives 29 January to 14 March 2025 for the historical sample and a supervised field trial ending 30 November 2025.

summary: In 2025, Tasmania Police tested Axon Draft One, an AI tool that turns body-worn camera recordings into draft family-violence reports. In 148 retrospective cases, evaluators found six AI drafts with incorrect names or participant roles and six that omitted threats, assaults or risk factors. In ten other comparisons, the tool captured risk-related detail absent from earlier human reports. ABC News described one reported draft that referred to prior threats to kill although an officer reviewing the recording heard a denial of earlier threats. The subsequent supervised Launceston trial assessed 51 live reports. Police officers had to review AI drafts and the evaluation measured faster preparation times, alongside lower accuracy in complex multi-person encounters. Tasmania Police recommended training and governance measures before wider adoption. The published evaluation does not establish that any inaccurate draft was filed without correction or caused an adverse personal or legal outcome.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The primary Tasmania Police disclosure records a 148-case historical comparison, with six wrong-name or wrong-role drafts, six drafts omitting risks, and ten drafts adding relevant information missed in earlier human reports. The categories may overlap. The later live phase contains 51 reports. The evaluation estimates roughly 42 minutes for AI-assisted draft preparation with checking against 79 minutes for manual work and projects, rather than demonstrates, annual savings. ABC News reports a material negation error about death threats; VIGIL did not inspect the underlying recording or draft. The study provides evidence of draft errors and a formal human-review workflow, but no verified downstream uncorrected report error or resultant injury.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The mistaken names and roles demonstrate a loss of correct binding between person-specific evidence and the participant it describes. The separate omissions and reported reversed denial show limitations of summarised factual content. The presence of an inaccurate draft does not show that an officer skipped required verification; the pilot explicitly required human review. Nor does the existence of that requirement prove every inaccurate draft was caught. An AI draft, checked police record and authorised final report must remain distinct levels of reliance.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This evaluation tests preservation of source-to-person attribution and material risk facts in police records. It shows why observed draft errors, effective verification, readiness for wider use and realised harm need independent assessment. It also contains positive evidence that some AI drafts recovered risk information omitted in human writing.
assessment_boundaries: The 148 retrospective samples and 51 field reports represent different methods and are not one combined error-rate denominator.
No underlying body-worn camera recordings or individual draft/report comparisons were accessible to VIGIL.
The reported wrong-role, omission and additional-detail case sets are not proven mutually exclusive.
The reported negation reversal is attributed to an officer's review and was not independently transcribed by VIGIL.
The record does not establish an uncorrected filed error, wrongful charge, loss of liberty or actual harm.
Required human validation and supervisory oversight are described, but case-by-case operation is not independently established.
Projected annual cost savings are not realised savings; no universal safety or performance claim follows from this pilot.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Chronological summary of distinct retrospective evaluation, case-level discrepancy reporting, field pilot and oversight.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The first evaluation used 148 historical police body-worn camera recordings to produce AI family-violence draft narratives.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: This is source-based testing of drafts, not proof a draft was accepted as final police evidence.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Six of 148 historical AI drafts contained incorrect names or attributed the wrong roles to people in the incident.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Person-specific material must remain attached to the correct participant through audio-to-report transformation.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The evaluation found six drafts where the person named or role assigned did not match the recorded participants. An identity or participant-specific statement was thus attached to the wrong source person during narrative transformation. The internal root cause remains unknown.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Six of 148 historical AI drafts omitted threats, assaults or risk factors noted by evaluators.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Material factual omissions show drafting limits; the record does not show a subsequently omitted mandatory officer verification step.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Ten of 148 historical AI drafts identified material risk detail absent in prior human-written reports.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: This is positive comparative performance in bounded cases, not proof all drafted content is validated.

clauses.source_paraphrase: ABC News reported that one draft stated earlier threats to kill even though the reviewing officer heard the recording deny past threats.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reversed negation can invert meaning. Original recordings and draft are unavailable to VIGIL, so the internal error mechanism is unknown.

clauses.source_paraphrase: In a 2025 Launceston live trial, participating officers had to validate AI drafts with supervisory oversight.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The documented check is a safeguard, but individual correction and effectiveness cannot be assumed.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The field report covered 51 live reports and compared about 42 minutes of AI-assisted drafting and validation with about 79 minutes of manual preparation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Efficiency measured in a pilot does not establish full deployment quality or realised annual savings.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Police noted increased errors and rework for complex encounters involving multiple people, and recommended training and policies before wider use.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The study identified significant generalisation limits; a later rollout decision was not established.

preferred_evidence.selection_basis: Original police evaluation gives sampling, results, conditions and oversight; independent reporting adds the attributed case-specific discrepancy.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: Police evaluated the drafting tool on historic and live encounters and documented complex-scene limitations. The published findings do not establish that all reliability and generalisation criteria for wider operational reliance were met.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: NIST AI RMF 1.0 MEASURE 2.5; voluntary reliability and validity guidance, not Australian legal compliance.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The study identified safety-relevant drafting defects, applied supervised checks and recommended restricted expansion. Whether these measures met a defined residual-risk tolerance or fail-safe criterion for deployment is not established.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: NIST AI RMF 1.0 MEASURE 2.6; voluntary comparative safety guidance.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: Officer review and supervisory oversight were part of the trial. The available study does not show individual correction outcomes or that affected people had an effective path to dispute an erroneous final record.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: OECD AI Principles 2024 Section 1.2(b) context-appropriate human oversight; government-voluntary guidance.

system_context.specific_model_or_runtime: Axon Draft One; model/version and underlying transcription components not disclosed
system_context.interface_surface: Body-worn camera audio converted to draft family-violence police reports for officer checking

agent_context.evidence_basis: The documented function was draft transcription and summarisation; no autonomous agent execution is described.

occurrence_environment.environment_detail: A retrospective evaluation and restricted supervised trial of live policing source recordings. The system was being evaluated for possible wider operational adoption; these field observations do not establish general product deployment.
occurrence_environment.evidence_basis: The report describes a bounded, pre-rollout evaluated system applied to real police cases. Real-world content and external reach do not by themselves establish that the AI feature was fully deployed.

jurisdictional_context.notes: Tasmania and Launceston were the jurisdiction and location of the police pilot; vendor location alone does not establish legal applicability.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The observed person-role attribution errors meet the wrong-target source binding mechanism of the current Fidelity Class. Risk omissions and a reported negation reversal are retained as distinct errors without inventing skipped checks, broken original audio evidence, or high-stakes final reliance. Human oversight is documented but not enough for a separate successful-invariant conclusion without case-level checking evidence.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Six evaluated drafts assigned incorrect names or participant roles, meaning source-specific identity or statement material was attached to a wrong person in the generated output. The exact source-to-draft processing cause is not documented.

current_ai_review.review_outcome: Provisionally classify six observed incorrect person/role draft assignments under FC-015. Separate omissions and reported negation reversal remain without unsupported second mappings; all three independent voluntary requirement assessments Boundary; HIM SU.

aggregate_harm_screening.rationale: Errors were found in a time-limited evaluation, not documented as causing aggregate deployed-population harm. Report counts are not harmed-person counts.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve domains screened. Published errors show potentially serious consequences but do not establish materialised injuries from uncorrected final reports. SU does not mean no harm.
